name: Krang Suri Falls
description: Stunning turquoise-blue waterfall in the Amlarem area of West Jaintia Hills, cascading into a natural pool amid dense forests. Popular for swimming, photography, and short treks; one of Meghalaya's most photogenic falls.
facts: About 30 km from Jowai and 85-90 km from Shillong
Height around 30 metres with striking blue-green water
Short trek of 10-20 minutes from parking
Best visited October to March for clearer views

name: Nartiang Monoliths
description: Largest concentration of ancient megalithic monoliths in Meghalaya, erected by Jaintia clans between the 16th and 19th centuries. Features towering menhirs and dolmens commemorating rulers and ancestors near Nartiang village.
facts: Tallest menhir about 8 metres high
Declared of national importance in 1958
About 25 km from Jowai
Largest single collection of monoliths in the region

name: Nartiang Durga Temple
description: Ancient Durga temple in Nartiang village, a Shakti Peeth associated with the Jaintia kingdom. Site of historical significance with local legends of past rituals; located near the famous monoliths.
facts: Over 600 years old according to local accounts
Linked to the summer capital of the Jaintiapur kingdom
About 25 km from Jowai near the monoliths
Active during festivals with local devotees

name: Thadlaskein Lake
description: Historic man-made lake near Mukhla village on NH-6, also known as Pung Sajar Nangli. Created according to folklore by Sajar Nangli and followers; popular for picnics, boating, and scenic views amid pine-covered hills.
facts: About 10-13 km from Jowai
Man-made according to local legend of overnight digging
On National Highway 6 near Mukhla
Also called Sajar Nangli Lake

name: Dawki and Umngot River
description: Border town and the crystal-clear Umngot River, famous for turquoise waters so transparent that boats appear to float in mid-air. Features the historic 1932 suspension bridge and India-Bangladesh border crossing.
facts: Umngot considered one of India's cleanest rivers
Historic British-era suspension bridge built in 1932
About 95 km from Shillong
Best clarity in winter months November to March

name: Shnongpdeng
description: Quiet riverside village upstream from Dawki on the Umngot, offering clearer waters, camping, kayaking, cliff jumping, and peaceful nature escapes away from border traffic. Ideal for overnight stays and adventure activities.
facts: About 8 km upstream from Dawki
Popular for riverside camping and water sports
Quieter alternative to Dawki town
Local Khasi community-run activities

name: Tyrshi Falls
description: Scenic multi-tiered waterfall near Jowai on the Shillong-Jowai road, accessible via an arched bridge over paddy fields. Offers panoramic valley views and is less crowded than more famous falls in the region.
facts: About 5 km from Jowai town
Connected by picturesque arched bridge
Short walk through paddy fields
Often compared to Elephant Falls but taller

name: Jowai Town
description: District headquarters of West Jaintia Hills and cultural hub of the Pnar people. Situated on a plateau at about 1,380 m, surrounded by the Myntdu River, serving as base for exploring waterfalls, monoliths, and lakes.
facts: Headquarters of West Jaintia Hills district
Elevation around 1,365-1,380 metres
About 64 km from Shillong
Home to Pnar sub-tribe of Khasi people

name: Ialong Park
description: Scenic park about 8 km from Jowai overlooking the Pynthorwah Valley, featuring sacred groves, walking paths, and panoramic views. Developed for tourism with picnic spots and natural surroundings.
facts: About 8 km from Jowai
Overlooks Pynthorwah Valley
Includes sacred grove areas
Ideal for short nature walks and views

name: Phe Phe Falls
description: Lesser-known waterfall near the Krang Suri route in West Jaintia Hills, requiring a short walk through rural paths. Offers layered cascades and quieter surroundings compared to more popular falls.
facts: Near the path toward Krang Suri Falls
Short rural walk required
Less crowded alternative waterfall
Surrounded by forest and rocks

name: Shillong
description: Capital city of Meghalaya and headquarters of East Khasi Hills district, known as the Scotland of the East. Nestled in pine-covered hills at about 1,500 m, it blends colonial architecture, vibrant markets, cafes, and access to nearby natural attractions.
facts: Headquarters of East Khasi Hills and state capital
Elevation around 1,496 m
Named after the deity Lei Shyllong
About 100 km from Guwahati

name: Shillong Peak
description: Highest point in Meghalaya at approximately 1,965 m, offering panoramic views of Shillong city, surrounding hills, and distant plains. Sacred to the Khasi people as the abode of Lei Shyllong; popular for sunset photography.
facts: Highest peak in the state at ~1,965 m
About 10 km from Shillong city centre
Requires photo ID for entry due to Air Force station
Best views on clear days

name: Elephant Falls
description: Three-tiered waterfall on the outskirts of Shillong, known locally as Ka Kshaid Lai Pateng Khohsiew. Cascades through lush greenery and fern-covered rocks; easily accessible with viewing platforms.
facts: About 12 km from Shillong city centre
Named after a rock that once resembled an elephant
Three successive falls with the third being the tallest
Short walk down steps from the road

name: Ward's Lake
description: Historic artificial horseshoe-shaped lake in the heart of Shillong, surrounded by botanical gardens, cobbled paths, and a wooden bridge. Ideal for boating, walks, and picnics amid flowering plants and pine trees.
facts: Built in 1894 by Colonel Hopkins under Sir William Ward
Locally known as Nan Polok or Pollock Lake
Near the Raj Bhavan in central Shillong
Features a central wooden bridge and orchid gardens

name: Don Bosco Museum
description: Don Bosco Centre for Indigenous Cultures in Mawlai, Shillong, one of Asia's largest museums dedicated to the cultures of Northeast India. Spans seven floors with galleries on tribes, artefacts, musical instruments, and traditional lifestyles.
facts: Located in Mawlai, about 3-6 km from Shillong centre
Opened in 2010; managed by Salesians of Don Bosco
Features 17 galleries on Northeast tribal cultures
Includes a skywalk with city views

name: Sohra (Cherrapunji)
description: Sub-divisional town in East Khasi Hills, formerly known as Cherrapunji, famous as one of the wettest places on Earth. Gateway to waterfalls, limestone caves, living root bridges, and views of the Bangladesh plains.
facts: Average elevation about 1,430 m
About 54-56 km from Shillong
Traditional capital of the Sohra Khasi kingdom
Record rainfall of over 26,000 mm in a year historically

name: Nohkalikai Falls
description: India's tallest plunge waterfall at 340 m (1,115 ft), plunging from the Sohra plateau into a turquoise pool. Associated with the Khasi legend of Ka Likai; dramatic cliffs and forests surround the site.
facts: Tallest plunge waterfall in India at 340 m
About 5-7 km from Sohra town
Fed by plateau rainwater; strongest in monsoon
Named from the legend of Likai

name: Nohsngithiang Falls (Seven Sisters)
description: Seven-segmented waterfall near Mawsmai village, cascading 315 m over limestone cliffs. Spectacular during monsoon when the segments stretch along the cliff face; viewpoint offers plains views.
facts: Height about 315 m with average width 70 m
About 1 km south of Mawsmai village
Best in full monsoon flow
Often paired with Mawsmai Cave visits

name: Mawsmai Cave
description: Short, accessible limestone cave near Sohra with lit passages, stalactites, and stalagmites. About 150 m of walkable route suitable for beginners; formed by chemical weathering of limestone.
facts: About 6 km from Sohra town, 58 km from Shillong
Route length around 150 metres
Open roughly 9:30 AM to 5:30 PM
Name means Oath Stone Cave in Khasi

name: Double Decker Living Root Bridge (Nongriat)
description: Iconic two-tier living root bridge in Nongriat village, grown from Ficus elastica roots by Khasi villagers over centuries. Requires a challenging trek of about 3,500 steps from Tyrna through rainforest.
facts: About 15 km from Sohra; trek starts at Tyrna
Estimated over 180-200 years old
UNESCO Tentative list as part of Jingkieng Jri landscapes
Supports dozens of people; stronger with age

name: Mawlynnong Village
description: Renowned as one of Asia's cleanest villages, featuring neat Khasi homes, bamboo dustbins, orchids, and a skywalk viewpoint toward Bangladesh. Near the India-Bangladesh border with a nearby single living root bridge at Riwai.
facts: About 90 km from Shillong near the border
Awarded cleanest village in Asia in 2003
100% literacy reported; community cleanliness tradition
Bamboo skywalk offers plains views

name: Laitlum Canyon
description: Dramatic canyon viewpoint near Smit, offering sweeping views of deep gorges, rolling green hills, and valley hamlets. Known as the end of the hills in Khasi; popular for photography and short treks.
facts: About 25 km from Shillong near Smit village
Name means end of the hills or slopes
Steep drops of hundreds of metres into the valley
Best visited on clear days for visibility

name: Mawphlang Sacred Forest
description: Ancient sacred grove (Law Lyngdoh) near Mawphlang village, preserved by Khasi tradition as the abode of the deity U Ryngkew U Basa. Dense primary forest with monoliths, orchids, and strict rule against removing anything.
facts: About 25 km from Shillong on the way to Sohra
Protected by traditional religious sanction for centuries
Guide mandatory; no removal of leaves or anything
Rich in orchids, rhododendrons, and medicinal plants
